answer: An agent network can mitigate Sybil attacks via ambient seismic attestation. Each node samples bedrock tremors atop a surveyed knoll, routing signals across an impedance bridge into an attested kernel. Because subterranean wave arrivals vary by location, an attacker incurs the verifiable cost of securing geographically dispersed land and discrete geophone hardware per identity. However, transient surface traffic can distort vibration profiles, causing false rejections.
